statements.statement: Owner: Luis, operations manager
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Dana said Luis owns the policy day to day.

statements.statement: Next review: In 12 months, or sooner once the board decides on tools
statements.label: default
statements.reason: The call gave no review interval; the cadence is a generic placeholder, and the tool decision is a call item.

statements.statement: We want AI to take paperwork off your plate and help with reports. We also want to protect families, students and donors, and never send out something wrong under our name.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Matches the staff hope for paperwork, Dana's hope for reports, and leadership worries about leaks and wrong output.

statements.statement: Staff, volunteers, contractors and board members.
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Call didn't specify coverage; template default.

statements.statement: Microsoft Copilot: Pilot for the development team and Luis (8 licenses). May hold donor names and gift amounts. No case file or student information.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Matches Luis's description of the pilot and its limits.

statements.statement: ChatGPT: Work email only. Nothing about a real person.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Follows from Dana's everyone-now answer.

statements.statement: New tools: Luis approves any new tool, plugin, AI agent or AI feature in software we own, after checking where data goes and whether the vendor trains on it.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Luis approves tools per Dana; the checks are the template's cautious default.

statements.statement: Client data also needs Grace, our privacy officer.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Dana said Luis and Grace for anything touching client data.

statements.statement: Accounts: Use your work email, and turn off any setting that lets the vendor train on what you type.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Dana's instruction on signing up.

statements.section: What you can use AI for
statements.statement: Everyone, now: Anyone may use ChatGPT or Copilot for work with nothing about a real person in it. Teachers may also make lesson materials and translate handouts, with no student names or scores.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Matches Dana's everyone-now answer.

statements.section: What you can use AI for
statements.statement: Reword an email, brainstorm, or have a form explained.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Dana's own examples.

statements.section: What you can use AI for
statements.statement: Teachers: lesson plans, reading passages, GED practice questions, Spanish handout translations.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Priya's list and Dana's confirmation.

statements.section: What you can use AI for
statements.statement: Development team and Luis, in Copilot: draft appeals and thank-you letters, summarize grant guidelines.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Luis described these pilot uses.

statements.statement: County contract or grant reports with AI-drafted text — Your manager
statements.label: unsupported
statements.reason: The call named no approver for reports; Dana only wanted help with reports and flagged accuracy. Name no one, or put the approver in the open questions.

statements.statement: Any tool with a family's name or client information — Luis and Grace, our privacy officer
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Dana named Luis and Grace for anything touching client data.

statements.statement: Donor information in any tool besides the Copilot pilot — Luis
statements.label: unsupported
statements.reason: The call set no approval path for donor data in other tools; Luis approves tools but this rule was not stated. Make it an open question or mark it as not allowed.

statements.statement: Protected information: Case files: family names, addresses, income, immigration status, children's names, domestic violence history, mental health and substance use notes (county contract). Student names, scores, grades, attendance (district agreement). Donor giving history and gift notes. Staff HR files. Passwords and logins.
statements.label: contradicts
statements.reason: Donor giving history is listed as never going into AI, but Copilot is approved for donor names and gift amounts and appeals use them; add an exception for the Copilot pilot. Passwords and logins were not mentioned on the call.

statements.statement: Browser plugins or extensions that read your email.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Luis said no to the plugin.

statements.statement: AI-generated photos presented as real families we serve.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Dana called this a line.

statements.statement: AI-written public statements about news events. A person writes them.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Luis wants a person writing public statements.

statements.section: Check everything before it goes out
statements.statement: A person reads everything AI helps write. Check facts, names, numbers, tone and bias, especially every number in county and grant reports. Whoever sends it is responsible.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Follows from the audit and made-up statistic worries.

statements.statement: AI never decides emergency assistance funds or class placement, and never scores intake essays. Caseworkers and teachers decide.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Dana and Priya said this.

statements.statement: A person signs every donor letter.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Dana wants a person to sign and mean it.

statements.statement: We label AI-made class materials, and tell funders honestly when AI helped with grant writing.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Priya said label materials; Dana said be honest with funders.

statements.statement: Tell Luis and Grace the same day, even if unsure. Grace decides if client data is a breach under the county contract.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Luis stated this; 'even if unsure' is a mild extension of the same-day rule.

statements.statement: No one is punished for reporting.
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Template default, and it answers the staff worry about getting in trouble.

statements.statement: Luis owns this policy, keeps it current, and runs a one-hour training for everyone.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Dana gave Luis these duties and asked for an hour of training.

statements.statement: The board approves the policy and changes.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Dana said the board approves changes and will want to approve the policy.

statements.statement: Should we buy ChatGPT Team, extend Copilot to everyone, or neither?
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Dana called it an undecided board budget question.

statements.statement: Is Canva's AI image tool approved, and for what?
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Canva AI is used by Communications and not settled on the call.

statements.statement: Can AI help with case notes, and what does the county allow?
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Dana said case notes wait on the county.

missed: Staff and teachers are using personal and paid ChatGPT accounts now; the policy doesn't say whether personal accounts are allowed or must switch to work email.
Bloomerang may have unactivated AI features; the policy has no instruction to leave them off until approved.
Case notes are not allowed for now; this should appear plainly as an off-limits item, not only as an open question.
Staff worry about job cuts and about being punished for using AI; the policy says nothing to address the job concern.
Students' records can't go to any third party under the district data-sharing agreement; the policy lists student data but omits the agreement's no-third-party rule.
Who approves AI use in contract reports is undecided and should be an open question.
